newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech stock market pioneer found dead aged 37.
newsitem.headline: Czech stock market pioneer found dead aged 37.

text.p: Michael Hobbs, a U.S.-born founding partner of the Czech brokerage firm Atlantik Financni Trhy and one of the pioneers of the post-Communist market, was found dead in his Prague apartment, police said on Wednesday.

Prague police spokesman Josef Sulcek told Reuters that Hobbs, who was working closely with the Prague Stock Exchange on the creation of a Securities Exchange Commission, was found by colleagues in the bathtub of his company-owned flat last Thursday and had been dead for about one week.

Sulcek said that there were no signs of violence but that an official cause of death had not been determined because medical examiners cannot perform an autopsy until relatives arrive from the United States.

"(Foul play) was ruled out but the cause of death -- whether it was heart failure or anything else... (the doctors) did not dare to estimate, because of the condition of the body, until after the autopsy," Sulcek said.

Prague Stock Exchange Chairman Tomas Jezek, who has been fighting a battle with the government to set up a securities watchdog akin to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), said Hobbs shared a passion for cleaning up the Czech markets during their work together.
"I am surprised and shocked by this news because I very highly appreciated the person of Michael Hobbs," Jezek said.
Hobbs, a native of San Diego and Yale University graduate, came to the former Czechoslovakia in 1991 to teach finance at Masaryk University in the Czech second city of Brno.

There he co-founded Atlantik in 1993 along with his former students Daniel Gladis and Karel Bastl, setting up a thriving business alongside the country's massive post-Communist privatisation programme.

Last summer, Hobbs resigned his executive position in the company after he said his partners had called an extraordinary shareholders' meeting of the limited liability company to strip him of his authority.
Hobbs said at the time that he would still hold on to his one-third share in Atlantik.

Gladis, contacted by telephone on Wednesday at Atlantik headquarters, said Hobbs had still been participating in shareholders' meetings and had looked healthy at a meeting in Brno on June 16, four days before the estimated date of his death.
Colleagues in the Prague investment community said Hobbs had remained active in Czech securities since leaving Atlantik.
